title: Fall of Constantinople (1453)
key_facts: Ottoman conquest of Byzantine capital ended the Byzantine Empire
Sultan Mehmed II's forces breached the massive Theodosian Walls
Marked the end of the Roman Empire's Eastern continuation
Led to Greek scholarly exodus to Western Europe, fueling the Renaissance
causes: Ottoman military superiority with cannons and gunpowder weapons
Byzantine Empire's long decline and territorial losses
Strategic importance of Constantinople as trade and cultural hub
Failure of Western European powers to provide effective aid
outcome: Constantinople renamed Istanbul and became Ottoman capital
End of the Byzantine Empire after nearly 1,100 years
Ottoman control over key trade routes between Europe and Asia
Mass migration of Greek intellectuals and scholars to Italy

figures.name: Mehmed II
figures.role: Ottoman Sultan who conquered the city

impacts: Ended the Byzantine Empire and Roman imperial continuity
Accelerated Ottoman expansion into Southeastern Europe
Catalyzed the Renaissance through Greek scholarly migration
Established Ottoman control over strategic Mediterranean trade routes
